idiom_name: Pekko/Akka typed actor: Behaviors.receive + replyTo ActorRef
implementation_notes: The actor is the endpoint: its behavior function receives each message from the mailbox, invokes the service logic and answers the sender through the ActorRef carried in the message, which is the pattern's request-reply form. Pekko's typed API documents message protocols and one-message-at-a-time processing, so the mailbox and the behavior replace the classic dispatcher and handler structure. Streams are the alternative when the messages form a flow rather than a sequence of commands: Source.queue + runForeach. Hand-written consumer loops remain justified for transports without an actor or streams integration.
pitfalls: Blocking inside receive (Await, JDBC, Thread.sleep) starves the dispatcher shared with other actors; use context.pipeToSelf with a Future instead.
Mailboxes are unbounded by default, so a slow service turns the actor into an out-of-memory queue; bound the mailbox or use stream backpressure.
The ask pattern allocates a temporary actor per request and fails with AskTimeoutException; it should not be the default way to invoke the service.
